Row and column operations

Source: R/matgeo-matrices.R
row_insert.Rd

Functional versions of SymPy's Matrix row and column methods. Indices are 1 based, as everywhere in R. row_insert() and col_insert() insert the rows or columns of other before position pos; row_del() and col_del() delete one; row_join() and col_join() concatenate; extract() picks rows and columns; permute(), permute_rows() and permute_cols() apply a permutation given as a list of swaps or as an image vector (a SymPy Permutation is taken 0 based); elementary_row_op() and elementary_col_op() apply "n->kn", "n<->m" or "n->n+km"; row_swap() and col_swap() swap two rows or columns. diagonal(), upper_triangular() and lower_triangular() take the kth diagonal and the triangles; vech() stacks the lower triangle; rot90() rotates; mat_row(), mat_col(), tolist() and matrix_values() read entries; multiply_elementwise() is the Hadamard product.

Usage

row_insert(M, pos, other)

col_insert(M, pos, other)

row_del(M, i)

col_del(M, j)

row_join(M, other)

col_join(M, other)

extract(M, rows, cols)

permute(M, perm, orientation = "rows", direction = "forward")

permute_rows(M, perm, direction = "forward")

permute_cols(M, perm, direction = "forward")

elementary_row_op(
  M,
  op = "n->kn",
  row = NULL,
  k = NULL,
  row1 = NULL,
  row2 = NULL
)

elementary_col_op(
  M,
  op = "n->kn",
  col = NULL,
  k = NULL,
  col1 = NULL,
  col2 = NULL
)

row_swap(M, i1, i2)

col_swap(M, i1, i2)

diagonal(M, k = 0)

upper_triangular(M, k = 0)

lower_triangular(M, k = 0)

vech(M, diagonal = TRUE, check_symmetry = TRUE)

rot90(M, k = 1)

mat_row(M, i)

mat_col(M, j)

tolist(M)

matrix_values(M)

multiply_elementwise(M, other)

Arguments

M

A symmatrix.

pos, i, j, i1, i2

Positions (1 based).

other

A symmatrix.

rows, cols

Row and column indices, or logical vectors.

perm

A list of swaps, an image vector or a Permutation.

orientation

"rows" or "cols".

direction

"forward" or "backward".

op

The elementary operation.

row, col, row1, row2, col1, col2

The rows or columns it acts on.

k

A scale factor, or for diagonal() and the triangles the offset of the diagonal; for rot90() the number of quarter turns.

diagonal

For vech(): include the diagonal.

check_symmetry

For vech(): require a symmetric matrix.

Value

A symmatrix (tolist() and matrix_values() return lists).

Examples

M <- Matrix(list(list(1, 2), list(3, 4)))
row_insert(M, 2, Matrix(list(list(0, 0))))
#> Matrix(3, 2)
#> [1, 2]
#> [0, 0]
#> [3, 4]
col_del(M, 1)
#> Matrix(2, 1)
#> [2]
#> [4]
permute_rows(M, list(list(1, 2)))
#> Matrix(2, 2)
#> [3, 4]
#> [1, 2]
elementary_row_op(M, "n->n+km", row = 2, k = -3, row2 = 1)
#> Matrix(2, 2)
#> [1, 2 ]
#> [0, -2]
diagonal(M)
#> Matrix(1, 2)
#> [1, 4]
